subject: ica
question: Under Section 2(a) of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, when one person signifies to another his willingness to do or to abstain from doing anything, with a view to obtaining the assent of that other to such act or abstinence, he is said to make a:
explanation: Section 2(a) defines a proposal (offer) in these terms. When the person to whom the proposal is made signifies his assent, the proposal is said to be accepted (Section 2(b)), and a proposal when accepted becomes a promise.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 2(h) of the Indian Contract Act, a contract is:
options: any promise made by one person to another
explanation: Section 2(h) defines a contract as an agreement enforceable by law. An agreement (Section 2(e)) is every promise and every set of promises forming the consideration for each other; only those satisfying Section 10 are enforceable by law.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act, all agreements are contracts if they are made:
options: between persons above twenty-one years of age
by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not expressly declared void
explanation: Section 10 lists the essentials of a valid contract: free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration, lawful object, and not being expressly declared void. Writing, registration or witnesses are required only where a particular law so provides.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, every person is competent to contract who:
options: is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject
has completed sixteen years of age
is literate and of sound mind
explanation: Section 11 makes a person competent to contract if he is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject. Under the Indian Majority Act, 1875, majority is ordinarily attained at eighteen.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 2(d) of the Indian Contract Act, consideration may move from:
options: the promisee or any other person, at the desire of the promisor
only a person who is a party to the contract
explanation: Section 2(d) provides that when, at the desire of the promisor, the promisee or any other person has done or abstained from doing, or does or abstains from doing, or promises to do or abstain from doing something, such act, abstinence or promise is consideration. Unlike English law, consideration may move from a third person.

subject: ica
question: Which of the following does NOT vitiate free consent under Section 14 of the Indian Contract Act?
explanation: Section 14 provides that consent is free when not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake. Inadequacy of consideration does not by itself make an agreement void, though the court may take it into account in deciding whether consent was freely given (Explanation 2 to Section 25).

subject: ica
question: Committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code, or unlawfully detaining or threatening to detain any property, to the prejudice of any person, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement, is defined in Section 15 as:
explanation: Section 15 defines coercion in these terms; its Explanation makes it immaterial whether the Indian Penal Code is in force where the coercion is employed. Undue influence (Section 16) involves a person in a position to dominate the will of another using that position to obtain an unfair advantage.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, agreements by way of wager are:
options: voidable at the option of the loser
valid if the amount is below one thousand rupees
explanation: Section 30 declares agreements by way of wager void, and no suit lies to recover anything alleged to be won on a wager or entrusted to a person to abide by its result. An exception saves subscriptions for a plate, prize or sum of money of five hundred rupees or more to be awarded to the winner of a horse-race.

subject: ica
question: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void, and a contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible or unlawful becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. This is provided by:
explanation: Section 56 embodies the doctrine of frustration (supervening impossibility). Its third paragraph requires a promisor who knew, or with reasonable diligence might have known, of the impossibility to compensate the promisee for loss sustained through non-performance.

subject: ica
question: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from the breach or which the parties knew when they made the contract to be likely to result from the breach, is provided for in:
explanation: Section 73 entitles the party suffering from a breach to compensation for loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things or which the parties knew, when contracting, to be likely to result from the breach. Such compensation is not given for remote and indirect loss, reflecting the rule in Hadley v. Baxendale.

subject: ica
question: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself or of any other person is called, under Section 124, a contract of:
explanation: Section 124 defines a contract of indemnity in these terms. A contract of guarantee (Section 126) is a contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default.

subject: ica
question: In a contract of guarantee under Section 126, the person in respect of whose default the guarantee is given is called the:
explanation: Section 126 provides that the person who gives the guarantee is the surety, the person in respect of whose default it is given is the principal debtor, and the person to whom it is given is the creditor. A guarantee may be either oral or written.

subject: ica
question: The delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, upon a contract that they shall, when the purpose is accomplished, be returned or otherwise disposed of according to the directions of the person delivering them, is defined in Section 148 as:
explanation: Section 148 defines bailment in these terms; the person delivering the goods is the bailor and the person to whom they are delivered is the bailee. A pledge (Section 172) is a bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise.

subject: ica
question: The bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called, under Section 172, a:
explanation: Section 172 defines pledge as the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise; the bailor is the pawnor and the bailee is the pawnee. A mortgage relates to immovable property and is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 182 of the Indian Contract Act, a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons, is called:
explanation: Section 182 defines an agent as a person employed to do any act for another or to represent another in dealings with third persons; the person for whom the act is done or who is represented is the principal. No consideration is necessary to create an agency (Section 185).

subject: ica
question: Under Section 2(g) of the Indian Contract Act, an agreement not enforceable by law is said to be:
explanation: Section 2(g) provides that an agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void. A voidable contract (Section 2(i)) is one enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties but not at the option of the others.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 7 of the Indian Contract Act, in order to convert a proposal into a promise, the acceptance must be:
explanation: Section 7 requires the acceptance to be absolute and unqualified and expressed in some usual and reasonable manner, unless the proposal prescribes the manner. A conditional acceptance or one varying the terms is a counter-proposal, not an acceptance.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 2(j) of the Indian Contract Act, a contract which ceases to be enforceable by law:
options: becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable
explanation: Section 2(j) provides that a contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be so enforceable. An example is a contract that becomes impossible to perform after it is made (Section 56).

subject: ica
question: Under Section 4 of the Indian Contract Act, the communication of an acceptance is complete as against the proposer:
options: when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer
when the acceptor decides to accept
when it is put in a course of transmission to him so as to be out of the power of the acceptor
explanation: Section 4 makes the communication of acceptance complete as against the proposer when it is put in a course of transmission to him so as to be out of the acceptor's power, and as against the acceptor when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer. Communication of a proposal is complete when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 5 of the Indian Contract Act, a proposal may be revoked:
options: at any time before the communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards
at any time before the acceptor's letter reaches the proposer
only with the consent of the person to whom it is made
at any time before the contract is performed
explanation: Section 5 allows a proposal to be revoked at any time before the communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards. An acceptance may be revoked at any time before its communication is complete as against the acceptor.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 6(4) of the Indian Contract Act, the death or insanity of the proposer revokes a proposal:
options: only if the fact of his death or insanity comes to the knowledge of the acceptor before acceptance
only if the proposal was made in writing
never; the proposal passes to the legal representatives
explanation: Section 6 lists the modes of revocation of a proposal: notice of revocation, lapse of the prescribed or a reasonable time, failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent, and the death or insanity of the proposer if that fact comes to the acceptor's knowledge before acceptance.

subject: ica
question: Under the exception to Section 19 of the Indian Contract Act, a contract whose consent was caused by misrepresentation or by silence fraudulent within Section 17 is NOT voidable if:
options: the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence
the contract was made in writing
the misrepresentation was made by an agent
the contract has been partly performed
explanation: Section 19 makes an agreement whose consent was caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Its exception provides that where consent was caused by misrepresentation or fraudulent silence, the contract is not voidable if that party had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence.

subject: ica
question: A agrees to buy from B a certain horse. It turns out that the horse was dead at the time of the bargain, though neither party was aware of the fact. Under Section 20 of the Indian Contract Act, the agreement is:
options: voidable at the option of A
valid, and B must supply another horse
valid, but B must pay damages
explanation: Section 20 provides that where both parties to an agreement are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void. The illustrations to Section 20 give the example of an agreement about a horse that, unknown to both parties, was already dead.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 21 of the Indian Contract Act, a contract caused by a mistake as to a law in force in India:
options: is void only if both parties were mistaken
explanation: Section 21 provides that a contract is not voidable because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India, but a mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact. The principle is that everyone is presumed to know the law of the land.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 25(1) of the Indian Contract Act, an agreement made without consideration is valid if it is expressed in writing, registered, and made on account of:
options: natural love and affection between parties standing in a near relation to each other
explanation: Section 25 declares agreements without consideration void, subject to three exceptions: (1) a written and registered agreement made on account of natural love and affection between parties in a near relation; (2) a promise to compensate a person who has voluntarily done something for the promisor; and (3) a written and signed promise to pay a time-barred debt.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 25(3) of the Indian Contract Act, a promise to pay a debt which the creditor might have enforced but for the law for the limitation of suits is valid if it is:
options: made in writing and signed by the person to be charged or his agent
oral and made before two witnesses
made within three years of the debt becoming time-barred
explanation: Section 25(3) validates a promise, made in writing and signed by the person to be charged or his authorised agent, to pay wholly or in part a debt which the creditor might have enforced but for the law of limitation. No fresh consideration is needed for such a promise.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 26 of the Indian Contract Act, every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is:
explanation: Section 26 declares void every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person other than a minor. Restraints on the marriage of minors are not covered by the section.

subject: ica
question: Under the exception to Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, an agreement in restraint of trade is valid where:
options: the seller of the goodwill of a business agrees with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business within specified local limits, so long as the buyer carries on a like business, provided the limits are reasonable
an employee agrees never to work for a competitor after leaving employment
a trader agrees not to carry on business anywhere in India
two traders agree to fix prices
explanation: Section 27 declares void every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind. The exception saves an agreement by the seller of the goodwill of a business not to carry on a similar business within specified local limits, so long as the buyer carries on a like business, if the limits are reasonable.

subject: ica
question: An agreement by which a party is absolutely restricted from enforcing his rights under a contract by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals is void under Section 28. Which of the following is saved by the exceptions to Section 28?
options: A contract by which disputes that may arise are to be referred to arbitration
A clause excluding all courts from deciding any dispute
A clause reducing the limitation period for suits to thirty days
A clause extinguishing a party's rights if he does not sue within six months
explanation: Section 28 voids agreements absolutely restricting enforcement of rights by legal proceedings, or limiting the time within which rights may be enforced, or extinguishing rights on expiry of a specified period. Its exceptions save contracts to refer to arbitration disputes that may arise, and contracts to refer questions that have already arisen.

subject: ica
question: A agrees to sell to B "a hundred tons of oil", and nothing shows what kind of oil was intended. Under Section 29 of the Indian Contract Act, the agreement is:
options: valid, and A may supply any oil
valid if B pays in advance
explanation: Section 29 declares void agreements whose meaning is not certain or capable of being made certain. The illustration to Section 29 uses this very example; but if A were known to deal only in coconut oil, the meaning would be capable of being made certain and the agreement would be valid.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 32 of the Indian Contract Act, a contingent contract to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens:
options: cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened, and becomes void if the event becomes impossible
can be enforced only after one year
explanation: Section 32 provides that contingent contracts dependent on the happening of an uncertain future event cannot be enforced unless and until that event has happened, and become void if the event becomes impossible. Section 33 deals with contracts contingent on an event not happening.

subject: ica
question: A agrees to pay B one lakh rupees if two straight lines should enclose a space. Under Section 36 of the Indian Contract Act, the agreement is:
options: void, because it is contingent on an impossible event
explanation: Section 36 declares void contingent agreements to do or not to do anything if an impossible event happens, whether or not the impossibility was known to the parties when the agreement was made. The illustration to Section 36 includes this example of two straight lines enclosing a space.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 39 of the Indian Contract Act, when a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee:
options: may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified by words or conduct his acquiescence in its continuance
must wait until the date of performance before suing
explanation: Section 39 deals with anticipatory breach: when a party refuses to perform or disables himself from performing his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract unless he has acquiesced in its continuance. He may also claim compensation for the breach under Section 75.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 55 of the Indian Contract Act, where a party fails to do a thing at or before a specified time, and the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract becomes:
options: voidable at the option of the promisee
explanation: Section 55 makes the contract, or so much of it as remains unperformed, voidable at the option of the promisee where time was of the essence. Where time was not of the essence, the contract does not become voidable, but the promisee is entitled to compensation for loss caused by the failure.

subject: ica
question: If the parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, the original contract need not be performed. This is provided by Section 62, which deals with:
explanation: Section 62 provides that if the parties agree to substitute a new contract, or to rescind or alter the existing one, the original contract need not be performed. Section 63 deals separately with the promisee's power to dispense with or remit performance.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 64 of the Indian Contract Act, when a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it:
options: the other party need not perform any promise, and the party rescinding must restore any benefit he has received under the contract to the person from whom it was received
the party rescinding may keep all benefits received
the other party must pay double damages
explanation: Section 64 relieves the other party of the need to perform his promises on rescission, but requires the party rescinding, if he has received any benefit under the contract, to restore it, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received. Section 65 imposes a similar duty when an agreement is discovered to be void or a contract becomes void.

subject: ica
question: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under it is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it. This rule is in:
explanation: Section 65 imposes the obligation to restore or compensate for any advantage received under an agreement discovered to be void or a contract that becomes void. The illustrations include money paid for a promise to marry a person who died before the promise was performed.

subject: ica
question: If a person incapable of entering into a contract, or anyone whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who furnished the supplies is entitled under Section 68 to:
options: be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person
sue the incapable person personally for the price
nothing, because the agreement is void
double the value of the supplies
explanation: Section 68 entitles a person who supplies necessaries suited to the condition in life of a person incapable of contracting (such as a minor) to be reimbursed from that person's property. There is no personal liability of the incapable person; the claim lies only against his property.

subject: ica
question: A tradesman leaves goods at B's house by mistake. B treats the goods as his own and uses them. Under Section 70 of the Indian Contract Act, B is:
options: not bound to pay, as there was no contract
bound to pay A for the goods, since A did not intend to act gratuitously and B enjoyed the benefit
bound only to return the goods, even if consumed
explanation: Section 70 provides that where a person lawfully does anything for another, or delivers anything to him, not intending to do so gratuitously, and the other enjoys the benefit, the latter is bound to compensate the former or restore the thing. The illustrations to Section 70 include goods left at the wrong house and used by the recipient.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 71 of the Indian Contract Act, a person who finds goods belonging to another and takes them into his custody is subject to the same responsibility as:
explanation: Section 71 subjects a finder of goods who takes them into his custody to the same responsibility as a bailee. Under Section 168, the finder may sue for a specific reward offered by the owner, and may retain the goods until he receives it.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 72 of the Indian Contract Act, a person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion:
options: may keep it if he acted in good faith
explanation: Section 72 requires a person to whom money has been paid or anything delivered by mistake or under coercion to repay or return it. The illustrations include payment of money by both A and B, each believing he was liable, and payment made under coercion to a railway company to deliver goods.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, where a contract names a sum to be paid in case of breach, or contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled:
options: whether or not actual damage or loss is proved, to receive reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or the penalty stipulated
to the full sum named in all cases
to the sum named only if he proves the exact loss
explanation: Section 74 entitles the aggrieved party, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved, to reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named or the penalty stipulated. Indian law thus does not follow the English distinction between liquidated damages and penalties; the named sum is the ceiling.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, the liability of the surety, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract, is:
options: secondary and arises only after the creditor exhausts remedies against the principal debtor
co-extensive with that of the principal debtor
greater than that of the principal debtor
explanation: Section 128 makes the liability of the surety co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless the contract otherwise provides. The creditor may therefore proceed against the surety without first suing the principal debtor.

subject: ica
question: A continuing guarantee may, under Section 130 of the Indian Contract Act, be revoked by the surety:
options: at any time, as regards all past and future transactions
at any time, as regards future transactions, by notice to the creditor
only with the consent of the principal debtor
only on the death of the creditor
explanation: Section 130 allows a continuing guarantee (one extending to a series of transactions, Section 129) to be revoked by the surety at any time as to future transactions, by notice to the creditor. The surety remains liable for transactions entered into before the notice.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 133 of the Indian Contract Act, any variance made without the surety's consent in the terms of the contract between the principal debtor and the creditor:
options: has no effect on the surety's liability
discharges the surety as to transactions subsequent to the variance
discharges the surety as to all transactions, past and future
explanation: Section 133 provides that any variance made without the surety's consent in the terms of the contract between the principal debtor and the creditor discharges the surety as to transactions subsequent to the variance. The surety remains liable for transactions before it.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 151 of the Indian Contract Act, the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as:
options: a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value
is necessary to prevent any loss whatever, as an insurer
explanation: Section 151 requires the bailee, in all cases of bailment, to take as much care of the goods as a man of ordinary prudence would take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value under similar circumstances. Under Section 152, a bailee who has taken that care is not responsible for loss, destruction or deterioration, in the absence of a special contract.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 171 of the Indian Contract Act, which of the following may, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, retain as security for a general balance of account any goods bailed to them (a general lien)?
options: Bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys of a High Court and policy-brokers
explanation: Section 171 gives a general lien to bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys of a High Court and policy-brokers, in the absence of a contract to the contrary. Other bailees have only a particular lien under Section 170 for services involving the exercise of labour or skill on the goods bailed.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 176 of the Indian Contract Act, if the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt at the stipulated time, the pawnee may:
options: sell the goods immediately without notice
bring a suit against the pawnor and retain the goods as collateral security, or sell the goods after giving the pawnor reasonable notice of the sale
keep the goods as his own without accounting
only sue for the debt, not sell
explanation: Section 176 allows the pawnee, on the pawnor's default, to sue on the debt and retain the goods as collateral security, or to sell the goods after reasonable notice to the pawnor. If the proceeds are less than the amount due, the pawnor remains liable for the balance; any surplus must be paid to him.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 16(3) of the Indian Contract Act, where a person in a position to dominate the will of another enters into a contract with him, and the transaction appears on the face of it or on the evidence to be unconscionable, the burden of proving that the contract was not induced by undue influence lies on:
options: the person whose will was dominated
the person in a position to dominate the will of the other
explanation: Section 16(3) shifts the burden of proving the absence of undue influence onto the party in a position to dominate the will of the other where the transaction appears to be unconscionable. Section 16(2) lists situations where such a position is deemed to exist, such as real or apparent authority, a fiduciary relation, or dealing with a person whose mental capacity is affected.

subject: ica
question: Under the Explanation to Section 17 of the Indian Contract Act, mere silence as to facts likely to affect a person's willingness to enter into a contract is NOT fraud, unless:
options: the circumstances are such that it is the duty of the person keeping silence to speak, or his silence is in itself equivalent to speech
the other party is a minor
the value of the contract exceeds one lakh rupees
explanation: The Explanation to Section 17 provides that mere silence is not fraud unless, having regard to the circumstances, it is the duty of the person keeping silence to speak, or unless his silence is in itself equivalent to speech. The illustrations distinguish a seller who simply stays silent from one in a fiduciary relationship with the buyer.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 24 of the Indian Contract Act, if any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful:
options: only the unlawful part is void
the agreement is voidable at the option of the innocent party
the agreement is valid if the lawful part is greater
explanation: Section 24 declares the agreement void where any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or part of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful. The illustration is a promise to superintend a legal manufacture of indigo together with an illegal traffic in other articles, for a single annual salary.

subject: ica
question: A, B and C jointly promise to pay D three thousand rupees. Under Section 43 of the Indian Contract Act, in the absence of an express agreement to the contrary, D:
options: must sue all three together and recover one thousand from each
may compel any one or more of them to perform the whole promise
may recover only from A, the first named promisor
may recover only in proportion to their property
explanation: Section 43 allows the promisee, in the absence of express agreement to the contrary, to compel any one or more of the joint promisors to perform the whole promise. A joint promisor who performs may then compel the others to contribute equally, and if one makes default, the others bear the loss in equal shares.

subject: ica
question: A person who is interested in the payment of money which another is bound by law to pay, and who therefore pays it, is entitled under Section 69 of the Indian Contract Act to:
options: a charge over all the other's property
explanation: Section 69 entitles a person who is interested in the payment of money which another is bound by law to pay, and who pays it, to be reimbursed by that other. The illustration is a person who pays land revenue due from his landlord to prevent the sale of land in which he holds an interest.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 135 of the Indian Contract Act, the surety is discharged when the creditor, by a contract with the principal debtor:
options: makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor
accepts part payment from the surety
agrees with a third person, not the principal debtor, to give time
explanation: Section 135 discharges the surety where the creditor contracts with the principal debtor to make a composition with him, give him time or not sue him, unless the surety assents. Under Section 136, an agreement by the creditor with a third person (not the principal debtor) to give time does not discharge the surety.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 141 of the Indian Contract Act, if the creditor loses, or without the surety's consent parts with, any security that he held against the principal debtor at the time the contract of suretyship was entered into, the surety is:
options: discharged to the extent of the value of the security
liable to compensate the creditor for the lost security
explanation: Section 141 entitles the surety to the benefit of every security the creditor has against the principal debtor at the time of the suretyship, whether or not the surety knows of it. If the creditor loses or parts with such a security without the surety's consent, the surety is discharged to the extent of the value of the security.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 139 of the Indian Contract Act, the surety is discharged if the creditor:
options: does any act inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires, and the eventual remedy of the surety against the principal debtor is thereby impaired
fails to send the surety a copy of the account each year
grants the surety extra time to pay
sues the surety before the principal debtor
explanation: Section 139 discharges the surety where the creditor does any act inconsistent with the surety's rights, or omits to do an act his duty to the surety requires, and the surety's eventual remedy against the principal debtor is thereby impaired. The illustrations include a creditor who fails to take steps that the contract required, causing loss to the surety.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 184 of the Indian Contract Act, as between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent. However, a person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind:
options: cannot be appointed an agent at all
can become an agent, but is not responsible to his principal according to the provisions of the Act
is personally liable to third persons on contracts he makes
can act only with court permission
explanation: Section 184 provides that, as between principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent so as to be responsible to his principal. The principal is bound by the minor agent's acts towards third persons, but cannot hold the minor liable for misconduct.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 202 of the Indian Contract Act, where the agent has himself an interest in the property which forms the subject-matter of the agency, the agency:
options: can be terminated by the principal at any time
cannot, in the absence of an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of such interest
terminates automatically on the principal's death
explanation: Section 202 provides that an agency coupled with interest cannot, in the absence of an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of the agent's interest. The illustrations include an agent authorised to sell land and pay himself, out of the price, debts due to him from the principal; the authority survives the principal's death or insanity.

subject: ica
question: Under Section 200 of the Indian Contract Act, an act done by one person on behalf of another, without his authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages or of terminating any right or interest of a third person:
options: cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect
is void and cannot be ratified at all
binds the third person if ratified within thirty days
explanation: Section 200 bars ratification from giving such an act the effect of subjecting a third person to damages or terminating his right or interest. The illustration is an unauthorised notice to quit given by a person on behalf of the owner, which cannot be made valid by later ratification so as to bind the tenant.

subject: ica
question: An agreement entered into by a minor, such as a mortgage executed by a minor in favour of a moneylender, is under the Indian Contract Act:
options: voidable at the option of the minor
valid if the minor misrepresented his age
void ab initio, as a minor is not competent to contract under Section 11
valid if ratified by the minor on attaining majority
explanation: Reading Sections 10 and 11 together, the Privy Council in Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose (1903) held that a minor's agreement is void ab initio, not merely voidable. It follows that the minor cannot ratify it on attaining majority, and he is not estopped by having misrepresented his age.
